Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staged compatibility sanitization — region schedule & customer impact

Hi all,

Summary: We will be running a staged compatibility sanitization across US-dense regions on Tuesday 2026-11-17 between 02:00 and 06:00 UTC. This is a low-risk pass that includes targeted driver sanity checks, kernel compatibility validation, and a brief KV-cache warmup to ensure prefetched prefixes survive handoffs.

What to expect:
- Window: 2026-11-17 02:00–06:00 UTC (per-region staggered starts; see attached schedule).
- Impact: Most customers will see no disruption. A small subset (~0.5% of active connections) may experience transient increased tail latency (200–500ms) for 1–3 minutes during handoffs. There are no planned evictions outside maintenance canaries.
- Rollout approach: Canary -> fleet-handoff -> validation -> gradual expansion. We will run the canary in us-west-2 for 15 minutes, then proceed to other zones if health metrics are stable.
- Opt-out: If you must opt-out for the window, reply with the project/team name and an explanation; we'll evaluate case-by-case and confirm by EOD 2026-11-13.

Attachments: staged-compat-schedule.pdf (region-by-region start times) and ops-runbook_v2.docx (runbook + rollback steps).

Action items for you:
1) Please confirm whether you need to opt-out.
2) If you run long-running KV-dependent inference jobs, let us know which endpoints so we can allocate warm-cache canaries.

We aim to keep customer impact minimal and will share live dashboards during the window. If you have an on-call number you prefer we contact in case of unexpected regressions, include it in your reply.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

Jasmine — answering inline from runbook perspective.

> 1) For KV-cache warmup, can you confirm whether public prefixes will be preserved across the handoff?
We will preserve prefixes that are marked persistent in the routing table. The canary will validate prefix persistence; if the canary detects >0.2% loss of persistent prefixes, rollout will halt and we will execute rollback steps in ops-runbook_v2.docx.

> 2) If we opt-out, will that block any of the downstream canary checks or just exclude our tenancy from active rollforward?
Opting out excludes your tenancy from the active rollforward; it will not block canary checks. We still need telemetry from you to validate the canary (a minimal telemetry shard).

For Acme: we will reserve a warm-cache canary lane for job acme-batch-77 between 02:25–02:40 UTC. Please send the exact endpoint(s) (full path) you use for the job.

I'll prepare a short runbook snippet for Acme (prefix-preservation checklist) and drop it into the shared Google doc.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Hi everyone — quick update and confirmation.

1) Acme: we reserved the warm-cache canary lane for acme-batch-77. Please point the job to the same endpoint but add header X-Redwood-Canary: acme-77. We will monitor your prefix persistence and share metrics in the live dashboard.
2) Opt-outs: we received two opt-out requests so far (Novus Data and a small research tenant). Both are approved; they will be excluded from active rollforward. Opt-out does not delay broader canary validation.
3) Runbook changes: Marissa added the prefix-preservation checklist (see Google Doc link below). We removed a non-critical kernel probe to reduce noise during canary.

Live monitoring during the window will be available here: https://status.redwood.com/maintenance/2026-11-17 (we will post the canary health snapshot and per-region roll status). Postmortem & follow-up: we will publish a short writeup to the shared doc at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-redwood-maintenance-plan within 48 hours after the window.

If anyone needs a pre-window run through with the reliability team, we can set up a 30-min dry-run on Thursday 2026-11-12 — reply with your preferred time.

Thanks and appreciate the coordination —
